description: The Jacobian of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of a resistor network with respect to its edge conductances has one column per edge; the exponential growth of its condition number with the depth of the unknowns is the central finding of the companion preprints. title: The isothermal theorem of evolutionary graph theory for birth-death updating, kernel-checked in Lean 4: Moran fixation on strongly connected isothermal graphs and its stationary-selection generalization
description: We prove in Lean 4 (Mathlib) the sufficiency direction of the isothermal theorem of evolutionary graph theory for birth–death updating. A population sits on the nodes of a row-stochastic replacement matrix W; mutants have fitness r > 0, residents 1; a node is chosen to reproduce with probability proportional to its fitness (times a selection weight μi > 0) and its offspring replaces node j with probability Wij. If W is doubly stochastic (isothermal) and strongly connected and μ ≡ 1, then from every initial mutant set S the t-step probability of reaching the all-mutant configuration converges to the Moran value (1 − r−|S|)/(1 − r−n) (|S|/n if r = 1); for a single mutant at any node this is (1 − r−1)/(1 − r−n). The same limit is proved whenever μW = μ (stationary selection) and every proper non-empty set has an outgoing edge. Preregistration deviation. The preregistered wording ‘the number of mutants is a birth–death chain with ratio r’ is false as a Markov statement for the chain with holding. A kernel-checked counterexample on the isothermal 4-cycle (r = 2) shows that two configurations with two mutants each have increase probabilities 1/3 and 2/3.
